=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:1038-1042 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The structured-clarification-block detection regex still uses `/^\s*-\s*\*\*[A-Z]\*\*\s*[—–-]/`, so it misses newer bullet forms and keeps the old separator-class hazard.
  WHY: Reviewers agreed the heuristic diverged from the widened parser, and several called out the old separator class as a missed-detection/false-positive risk.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:1193 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The chord-capable capture group `([A-Za-z](?:\+[A-Za-z])*)` is more permissive than necessary and can match malformed chord-like input before later validation rejects it.
  WHY: Reviewers disagreed on whether this is a real bug, but both noted the downstream single-letter guard prevents runtime impact, so it is at most a low-severity hardening issue.
- tests/test_plan_auto_answer_recommended_parser.py:288-298 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The test checks `assert "**A** — \\<description\\> (RECOMMENDED)" in prompt`, which is the pre-existing escaped blockquote form, not the new canonical inline-code form.
  WHY: Most reviewers saw this as a coverage gap, while one reviewer said it would block CI on current prompts; use the highest stated severity.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:1038 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The structured-clarification-block detection regex still uses the old byte-class separator pattern `[—–-]` instead of the updated alternation form `(?:—|–|[-)\.:])`.
  WHY: If Codex emits non-bold, non-dash separator recommendation bullets and omits the `STATUS: NEEDS_CLARIFICATION` header, the structured-block detection would miss it; the mismatch is a maintenance hazard.
- tests/test_plan_auto_answer_recommended_parser.py:291-293 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The first assertion `assert "**A** — \\<description\\> (RECOMMENDED)" in prompt` matches the pre-existing blockquote text, not the newly added inline-code instruction text.
  WHY: If a future edit mangles the new canonical-form instruction while keeping "Each option line MUST be exactly", the test still passes because it only checks the old escaped form.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- tests/test_plan_auto_answer_recommended_parser.py:288-293 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test assertion searches for `"**A** — \\<description\\> (RECOMMENDED)"`, which matches the pre-existing escaped format and does not verify the newly added canonical-form instruction.
  WHY: The test passes but does not cover the new inline-code guidance, so a corrupted canonical-form instruction would not be caught.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:1038 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The structured-clarification-block detection regex still uses `[—–-]` and `\*\*[A-Z]\*\*`, so it is not updated to accept the new bullet formats.
  WHY: When Codex emits non-canonical bullet formatting, this backup detection path fails even though the main parser at line 1193 would succeed.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:1038 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The structured-clarification-block detection regex still requires bold uppercase `**A**` and only accepts dash separators `[—–-]`, while the parser now accepts additional formats.
  WHY: If Codex emits clarification questions like `- A) ...` or `- a. ...`, the detection heuristic can fail to recognize the structured block and the workflow may skip the auto-answer path.
- tests/test_plan_auto_answer_recommended_parser.py:293 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The assertion only verifies the old escaped placeholder form and does not check the newly added canonical-form instruction text.
  WHY: The test passes today because the old blockquote example still contains the escaped form, so it would not catch removal or corruption of the new inline-code guidance.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- tests/test_plan_auto_answer_recommended_parser.py:292 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `assert "**A** — \\<description\\> (RECOMMENDED)" in prompt` checks the pre-existing blockquote example, not the new canonical-form inline-code instruction.
  WHY: The assertion silently tests old text that remains in the prompts, so deleting or rewriting the new instruction would not be caught.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:1038 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The character class `[—–-]` in the detection regex contains multi-byte UTF-8 characters and is a byte-class hazard in Perl byte mode.
  WHY: The class can accidentally match by bytes rather than code points, creating false-positive risk in the structured-block heuristic.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:1193 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The chord capture group `([A-Za-z](?:\+[A-Za-z])*)` is more permissive than necessary and can overmatch malformed chord-like input.
  WHY: The downstream `$tokens[0] !~ /^[A-Z]$/` guard rejects non-single-letter tokens, so this does not create a runtime bug.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_1-fast ===
- tests/test_plan_auto_answer_recommended_parser.py:288-298 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Assert checks for old escaped placeholder `"\<description\>"` but prompts use unescaped `<description>` inside code spans.
  WHY: The test targets pre-existing text instead of the new canonical-form instruction, so it can fail to cover or validate the change.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:1038-1042 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The detection regex `/^\s*-\s*\*\*[A-Z]\*\*\s*[—–-]/` requires strict bold `**A**` and the old byte-class `[—–-]`, so it misses tolerated forms like `- A) ...`.
  WHY: The fallback heuristic is inconsistent with the widened parser and can miss structured clarification blocks when the output omits the status line.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:1193 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The capture `([A-Za-z](?:\+\+[A-Za-z])*)` is more permissive than needed and can match malformed chord-like input before downstream checks.
  WHY: The later validation rejects malformed tokens, so this is a hardening issue rather than a confirmed runtime bug.
=== END FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_1-fast ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5 ===
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:1041 | severity=medium
  PROBLEM: The `HAS_STRUCTURED_CLARIFICATION_BLOCK` detection heuristic uses a stricter regex than the main auto-answer parser and misses noncanonical clarification bullets.
  WHY: If Codex emits a new-format clarification block without a `STATUS: NEEDS_CLARIFICATION` line, `needs_clarification` can stay false and the workflow can skip parsing.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:1041 | severity=medium
  PROBLEM: The `[—–-]` separator class in the detection regex is a byte-class hazard in byte-mode Perl.
  WHY: The multi-byte characters decompose into matching bytes, which can create false positives in the heuristic.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5 ===
